19.12 W02 · End-to-end field-to-sky replay
W02 replayed the Malta workflows on the archived 2.0.9004 build and on the final build, with intermediate tables for field reduction, sightlines, transformed densities, inference, screening, seasonal dates, crossings and reconstructed sky position. The Maltese entrances are published true bearings. The raw compass and solar-circle observations in this study are separately constructed controls. They do not reconstruct the original instrument notebooks.







Handoff
Result




Raw field controls
A target circle of 2.25° and solar circle of 358.75° give 161.23° at the Malta control site. The archived matrix call returned −558.77°, equivalent modulo 360°, and its single-vector call failed. In a two-site fixture the old matrix reshaping also changed the actual assigned coordinates. The corrected paired bearings were 161.23° and 141.72°, each matching the independent circle-difference calculation.


Mnajdra South
The edges 90.94° and 99.14° sampled skyline heights of 4.40° and 3.45°. The corresponding declinations were +1.71° and −5.48° on both builds. The first divergence along the published-bearing route was in the azimuth PDFs. The final 68% declination HDR comprised −4.75° to −1.95° and −0.90° to +1.00°.


Group inference
The replay preserved entrance/profile order for all 17 Ġgantija-phase entrances. The 39-simulation controls exercised both significance routes with fixed inputs and seeds. Separately, the full vignette replay used 500 random-orientation simulations and recovered the bundled global p = 2/501, the excess at −33.7° to −28.6° (adjusted p = 2/501), and the excess at −49.4° to −48.2° (adjusted p = 279/501).


Skorba West
Gacrux was returned by the screen for the archived significant band. The modeled heliacal rising date was 12 October 3250 BCE, Julian calendar. On the fifth subsequent morning the terrain crossing was at 03:33:11 UT and azimuth 129.9315°. Twenty minutes later the sketch placed Gacrux at azimuth 132.9940°, altitude 4.2488°, between the entrance edges 128.55° and 138.07° and 2.41° above the recorded skyline. A separate spherical transform at the saved instant reproduced the sketch coordinates.



Sensitivity. Swapping the Mnajdra South and Skorba West profiles changed only the corresponding two mean declinations, by 2.219° and 1.448°. The numeric calculation followed the supplied order, so correct site pairing remains the analyst’s responsibility. Rebuilding the PDFs with refraction off shifted their means by 0.146° on average. The seeded random test on the original stored PDFs retained its original results when the session setting changed. A north-crossing density integrated to one. An out-of-sector photographic transformation returned a finite curve on the archived build and an explicit coverage error on the final build.
All 26 workflow assertions passed, alongside the site-row and terminal-position controls. Agreement across this workflow establishes numerical continuity of its inputs and outputs. It provides neither a measurement of ancient naked-eye visibility nor evidence of intentional alignment. Download W02 scripts, per-stage tables and version comparisons.

title: 20  Checking the date of heliacal rising
text:
20.1 Sites, stars and epochs
Question. How close is the seasonal date from star.phases() to the first morning that a second visibility model puts the star above its detection threshold?
Finding. In 69 of 70 comparable cases, the two dates fell within one week of each other. The comparison uses modelled visibility at dawn. Assessing accuracy against what people actually saw would require dated naked-eye observations.
The main design crossed eight stars with five epochs (3500, 3250 and 2000 BCE, 200 and 2026 CE) and two horizons. Wiltshire used a level horizon at 51.18° N, 1.83° W. Mnajdra South used a terrain skyline from the package. The Mnajdra runs allowed all bearings and held the skyline fixed across epochs. The comparison makes no claim that either monument was in use throughout the sampled period.
Capella produced no heliacal-rising event in the ten site–epoch combinations. Its ten rows remain in the download with blank event dates. The resulting 70 comparisons represent seven stars. Five southern-star cases at Mnajdra form a separate follow-up and are excluded from the headline count.
crumbs: 20  Checking the date of heliacal rising

title: 20  Checking the date of heliacal rising
text:
20.2 Comparator and shared inputs
The reference date comes from star.phases(). The comparator searches mornings around that date on a one-minute grid. It evaluates extinction-adjusted point-source flux against the local background radiance, applying the point-source contrast threshold of Crumey (2014, eqs. 32–33). A minute above threshold qualifies. The search covered 24 days on either side of the reference date, extended to 64 days where necessary. The experiment therefore checks agreement near the selected event.
The two calculations share the site, ephemeris and stellar catalogue. The assumed central dark-sky limit was magnitude 6, extinction was 0.20 magnitudes per airmass, refraction was disabled and the Moon was hidden. The benchmark used the twilight and sky-brightness model in development build 2.0.9003. Its threshold is applied to radiance before display compression. It is a criterion used by this study.
